Fact.Description: §225(c)(1): "overtime compensation paid to an individual required under section 7 of the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 that is in excess of the regular rate". Asked when a W-2 has code TT. Placeholder false: no deduction unless confirmed.
Ask the unreported-overtime screener when the return has a W-2 or a Schedule C business.

#68: the filer had qualified overtime that isn't shown in W-2 box 12 code TT. Draft Form 1040 instructions (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040gi--dft.pdf), Schedule 1-A Part III, p.106: "If the amount of your qualified overtime compensation isn't separately identified on your Form W-2, Form 1099-NEC, or Form 1099-MISC, you can figure your qualified overtime compensation using one of the methods described in paragraphs 1 through 5." Placeholder false.
#68: overtime paid to the filer as a non-employee and reported on Form 1099-NEC or 1099-MISC (Schedule 1-A lines 18-19). Not computed: stop. Placeholder false.

#68: Draft Form 1040 instructions (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040gi--dft.pdf), Schedule 1-A Part III, p.106: "If your employer is covered by a different overtime rule in section 7 of the FLSA, rather than the general rule in section 7(a), you must compute your overtime compensation using the rule that applies to you" (e.g. public-sector fire protection or law enforcement, or compensatory time off). Not computed: stop. Placeholder false.

#68: the p.106 methods. statementPremium = paragraph 1 (statement shows the FLSA Overtime Premium, x 1); statementTotalTimeAndHalf = paragraph 2 (total pay for overtime hours at time-and-a-half, "divide the total amount by three (3)"); statementPremiumDoubleTime = paragraph 3 for double time (premium above the regular rate, x 1/2, Example 2: $10,000 premium gives $5,000); statementTotalDoubleTime = paragraph 4 for double time (total pay for overtime hours, x 1/4, Example 3: $20,000 gives $5,000); regularPayForOvertimeHours = paragraph 5 (regular rate x hours over 40, x 1/2: the "half" of time-and-a-half); other = any other premium rate or method: stop.
#68: which p.106 method fits the filer's records. See /overtimeMethodOptions.

#68: the amount for the chosen method, from the employer's statement, pay stubs or payroll records (or, for paragraph 5, regular hourly rate x hours worked over 40). p.106: "Make sure to keep a record of the documents you use when determining the amount of your qualified overtime compensation."

Fact.Name: Switch: draft 1040 instructions p.106 alternative overtime methods
Fact.Description: #68, ruling for TY2026: OFF. The p.106 methods are headed "Determining the amount of qualified overtime compensation for 2025. Because no changes have been made to Form W-2, Form 1099-NEC, or Form 1099-MISC to account for a separate accounting of qualified overtime compensation ..." (transition relief, Notice 2025-69), and §225(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/225) allows the deduction for overtime "included on statements furnished to the individual pursuant to section 6041(d)(4) or 6051(a)(19)". With the switch off, any qualified overtime not on W-2 code TT (including Form 1099 overtime) hits /flowKnockoutOvertimeNotComputable. Same role as /tipsSstbInterimRuleApplies. Placeholder false; no screen writes it (writable only so tests can turn it on). Turn on only if the TY2026 instructions keep the p.106 methods.

#68 polish: ask the Form 1099-NEC/MISC overtime question only when /overtimeAlternativeMethodsApply is on. Stop-only users (switch off for TY2026) already hit /flowKnockoutOvertimeNotComputable from /overtimeNotOnW2CodeTT alone via /flowIsKnockedOut, so they skip this screen. Draft Form 1040 instructions (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040gi--dft.pdf) p.106 alternative methods.

True when the method question is asked and answered "other". Complete false when it isn't asked (or the not-on-code-TT question is unanswered), so returns without self-figured overtime never wait on it.
§225(d): the return must include a valid SSN (§24(h)(7)). The self-figured amount isn't tied to one W-2, so every filer on the return must have one; otherwise stop.

Fact.Name: Knockout: qualified overtime this tool can't compute
Fact.Description: #68 replaces #59's stop for all overtime not on code TT. Stopped: everything while /overtimeAlternativeMethodsApply is off (TY2026); with it on, overtime on Form 1099-NEC/MISC, a special FLSA section 7 rule, a premium rate or method other than the p.106 paragraphs modeled, or a filer without a valid SSN. Wired into /flowIsKnockedOut in flow.xml.

#68: qualified overtime figured under p.106 paragraphs 1-5 (see /overtimeMethodOptions for each fraction). §225(c)(1): only the amount "in excess of the regular rate". Counted on line 17 with code TT (line 16 is the W-2 employee line), so the $12,500 / $25,000 cap and the phaseout apply to the total.

Line 17: add lines 16a-16e column (iii), qualified overtime of a W-2 employee: code TT plus, under #68, the amount figured with the draft 1040 instructions p.106 methods (/overtimeSelfFiguredAmount). Zero unless the FLSA premium is confirmed and not MFS (§225(e)). Per-W-2 valid SSN is applied in formW2s.
Line 21: "Enter the smaller of the amount on line 20 or $12,500 ($25,000 if married filing jointly)". Line 20 = line 17 + line 19 (0). §225(b)(1).
Line 23: "Enter $150,000 ($300,000 if married filing jointly)". §225(b)(2)(A).
Line 24: line 22 (= line 3 MAGI) minus line 23, not below zero.
Line 25: "Divide line 24 by $1,000. If the resulting number isn't a whole number, decrease the result to the next lower whole number." StepwiseMultiply = floor(x / 1000) x 1.
Line 26: "Multiply line 25 by $100".
Line 27: "Qualified overtime compensation deduction. Subtract line 26 from line 21. If zero or less, enter -0-". Complete 0 when there is no code TT or self-figured overtime.
